item.title: Photo of Jane Doe shared in Snapchat group on night of alleged rape
item.description: The photo was shared in a Snapchat group with dozens of Chi Phi fraternity brothers on the night the alleged victim says she was assaulted at Cornell.

item.title: Trump says Europe will release "massive amount" of diesel oil from stockpiles
item.description: A joint statement from G7 world leaders confirmed there will be a "coordinated release" of 100 million barrels, to begin "immediately."

item.title: $1.7 million raised in scheme for Hamas, including from U.S. donors, feds say
item.description: Saleem Alzaq, a 45-year-old Gaza man who prosecutors allege is a longtime Hamas member, was charged with helping operate the fundraising campaign claiming to provide humanitarian aid, according to an indictment.

item.title: Gypsy Rose Blanchard's partner, Ken Urker, dies at 34
item.description: Gypsy Rose Blanchard and Ken Urker connected while she was in prison for the 2015 murder of her mother, Clauddine "Dee Dee" Blanchard.

item.title: Americans donated money to Hamas in scheme that raised $1.7 million, prosecutors allege
item.description: Some donors in the U.S. contributed money for humanitarian aid after the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks that was later funneled to the terrorist group Hamas, prosecutors say. CBS News' Anna Schecter reports.

item.title: Cornell student body feels "let down" by university, student leader says
item.description: Adriana Vink said dozens of students attended a town hall to discuss the administration's response to campus sexual violence.

item.title: Trump vows Iran war to end "very quickly" as more troops head to Mideast
item.description: Some 9,000 more U.S. forces head for the Middle East as Trump vows the war will end "right after the election," if not sooner.

item.title: McMaster on Iran using proxies out of desperation, says conflict will persist if regime remains
item.description: Former Trump adviser, retired Lt. Gen. H.R. McMaster, joins CBS News with his take on the Iran war as the regime continues to use proxies in the Middle East and as President Trump seeks an end to the conflict.

item.title: Jane Doe's account of what happened at Cornell fraternity house
item.description: A former Cornell student, identified as Jane Doe, filed a civil lawsuit against the school and seven former fraternity brothers she accuses of rape and sexual assault.

item.title: In Cornell investigation, Gov. Hochul says AG James will find out "how was this woman denied justice"
item.description: Gov. Kathy Hochul has tapped New York Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor in the Cornell University alleged rape case.

item.title: Anne Hathaway enjoyed her "creepy and eerie" role in Colleen Hoover's "Verity"
item.description: Academy Award-winner Anne Hathaway is on a roll with five major films hitting cinemas this year. Her latest project is "Verity," an adaptation of Colleen Hoover's bestselling novel of the same name.

item.title: Alice Cooper warms up for his outrageous on-stage antics by throwing knives
item.description: Shock rocker Alice Cooper takes "CBS Mornings" behind the scenes and shares the characters who inspired his outrageous on-stage persona.

item.title: "Survivor" alum Rick Devens says he's not the "Sisyphus of reality TV" after "Big Brother" win
item.description: Two-time "Survivor" competitor Rick Devens just took the "Big Brother" crown after this season's grand finale. Devens joins "CBS Mornings" as he rejoices in his victory.

item.title: Is your job safe from AI? Mercor CEO Brendan Foody on the evolution of human work
item.description: Artificial intelligence is transforming the workplace, raising questions about the roles people will have in the future. Mercor CEO Brendan Foody says AI may change human work rather than simply replace it. Watch more of his interview Sunday on 60 Minutes.

item.title: Employers added 29,000 jobs in September, missing economic forecasts
item.description: Unemployment ticked up to 4.2% in September, while employers pulled back on hiring amid economic headwinds.

item.title: Astronaut will miss birth of child during ISS mission
item.description: Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk will be 260 miles away from Earth during the birth of his third child -- but he and his wife are feeling positive, despite their separation.

item.title: Questions emerge after Christa Pike's botched execution
item.description: Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike survived two doses of a lethal injection drug during her attempted execution, her attorneys say. Officials are investigating what went wrong.

item.title: Fisherman trapped under boulder saved after using Siri to call for help
item.description: A fisherman who was trapped under a boulder was rescued after he used his headphones to ask Siri to call 911. Carter Evans has more.

item.title: Amazon Prime customers could get $200 refunds in expanded FTC deal.
item.description: Some Amazon customers could receive refunds of up to $200. Here's who is eligible for a payment and when consumers will get the money.

item.title: White House reacts after mediocre jobs report
item.description: The U.S. economy added 29,000 jobs in September, a disappointing number for economists and forecasters. CBS News' Emily Pandise and Ed O'Keefe report.

item.title: Hochul on "troubling questions" in the Cornell rape case, says it exposes gap in state consent law
item.description: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul addressed the Cornell University gang rape allegations and said state Attorney General Letitia James will investigate the claims. Hochul also said the case is exposing a gap in state laws surrounding intoxication and consent. CBS News' Tom Hanson has more.

item.title: Border czar Homan responds to lawsuit by family of Renee Good, American killed by ICE agent
item.description: Renee Good, an American citizen, was shot and killed by an ICE agent in Minneapolis last winter. Now her family is suing the U.S. government. President Trump's border czar Tom Homan spoke with Camilo Montoya-Galvez about the case.

item.title: Ken Urker, Gypsy Rose's partner, dead at 34
item.description: Ken Urker, Gypsy Rose Blanchard's partner and the father of her daughter, has died at 34.

item.title: Trump campaigns in red states amid discontent over rising prices, Iran war
item.description: President Trump is on the campaign trail as he looks to shore up Republican support ahead of the midterm general election.

item.title: Hundreds of schools closed as fiery French student protests spread
item.description: French high school students light fires, clash with police as protests over school conditions leave more than 200 people wounded, force hundreds of schools to close.

item.title: Trump says Iran is "ready to fold up" but the U.S. is sending more troops to the Middle East
item.description: A third U.S. aircraft carrier is headed to the Middle East as President Trump claims that Iran is ready to surrender the war once the American midterms end. CBS News' Ramy Inocencio reports.

item.title: Patient dies by suicide after "insurance issue" delayed medicine
item.description: Hours after experiencing a flare-up related to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, Kenney Blewett of Kyle, Texas, died by suicide in June.

item.title: Cornell Title IX investigation docs reveal new details on rape investigation
item.description: CBS News has examined hundreds of pages of transcripts from the Title IX investigation conducted by Cornell University into the allegations made by a former student who claims she was drugged and gang-raped at a fraternity house.

item.title: Trump likely to pick Jay Clayton for AI czar, sources say
item.description: Jay Clayton will likely be the White House's pick for AI czar, and the Trump administration has been discussing having him remain in his current role as director of national intelligence, according to sources briefed on the matter.

item.title: U.S. layoffs drop nearly 40% in 2026 to 4-year low, new data shows
item.description: Hiring plans are up 3% so far this year, signaling the labor market remains resilient, experts say.
